Lesson 1 
Meaning of force and its measuring units 
Introduction to force 
When you kick the ball, you exert a force. When you sit in the chair, you exert a force. When 
you push or pull the door, you exert a force also. Push or pull of an object is considered a 
force. Push and pull come from the objects interacting with one another. So, forces describe

nteracting with one another. So, forces describe 
the interactions between an object and its environment. 
When there is an interaction between two objects, there is a force upon each of the objects. 
When the interaction vanishes, there is no force between the two objects. Forces only exist 
as a result of an interaction. 
The concept of force F 
 (An external effect that affects the object, it changes or attempts to change its state or 
direction). 
 (An action which produces or tends to pro

ion). 
 (An action which produces or tends to produce a change in a body’s state of rest or 
motion). 
Effects of the Force 
The Force has different effects such as 
a) The Force can make a body that is at rest to move. 
b) The Force can stop a moving body or slow it down. 
c) The Force can accelerate the speed of a moving body. 
d) The Force can change the direction of a moving body along with its shape and size. 
 
Types of forces: 
Force can be classified into two broad categories 
A) Contac

be classified into two broad categories 
A) Contact forces 
These types of forces are produced when two objects interact with each other; they have a 
physical contact with each other 
Examples of contact forces 
a) Frictional force 
b) Tension force 
c) Normal Force 
d) Air Resistance Force 
e) Applied Force 
f)  Spring Force 
B) Action at a distance force (Non-Contact forces) 
These types of forces happen when two interactive objects are not in physical contact with 
each other. 
Examples of A

each other.

a) Gravitational force 
b) Electrical force 
c) Magnetic forces

Lesson 2 
Gravitational force   
What Is Gravity? 
Gravity is the force by which a planet or other body draws objects toward its center. The 
force of gravity keeps all of the planets in orbit around the sun. 
What else does gravity do? 
Why do you land on the ground when you jump up instead of floating off into space?  
Why do things fall down when you th

into space?  
Why do things fall down when you throw them or drop them?  
The answer is gravity that is an invisible force that pulls objects toward each other.  
Anything that has mass also has gravity. Objects with more mass have more gravity. 
Gravity also gets weaker with distance. 
Gravity is very important to us. We could not live on Earth without it. The sun's gravity 
keeps Earth in orbit around it .

Motion in a circle (motion that repeats itself at equal intervals of time such as the motion of 
the Earth around its axis and also around the sun) is one of the most important common

motion of Earth around the Sun, the moon ar

number of its life examples, deducing the mathematical relations used to express it, and 
demonstrating most important life and technological applications.

It is necessary to calculate the centripetal force when designing a curve in roads or railways 
in order to help cars and trains move along this curved path without skidding.  
Through studying the relation, we can conclude that the centripetal force depends on each of

move along some dangerous curves.

of velocity at constant (r , m). When the velocity of a car incre

curves.

Lesson 4 
Friction force 
Introduction  
As an object moves across a surface it causes friction. 
Friction force can be sliding or static. Friction depends 
upon the nature of the two interacting surfaces. Such as  
1) A book sliding on the table, 
2) A ball rolling on the floor. 
Concept of friction 
Friction is the force that resists motion when the s

iction is the force that resists motion when the surface 
of one object comes in contact with the surface of 
another. 
Frictional force is the force generated by two surfaces that contact and slide against each 
other.  
Frictional force is the force that resists the sliding or rolling of one solid object over another 
The factors affecting the frictional force: 
a) The force with which the two surfaces are pressed together 
b) The nature of the two surfaces that are sliding across each other

two surfaces that are sliding across each other 
c) The angle and position of the object  
1) If an object is placed flat against an object, then the frictional force will be equal to 
the weight of the object 
2) If an object is pushed against the surface, then the frictional force will be increased 
and becomes more than the weight of the object  
Types of friction force  
Friction is the force that opposes motion between any surfaces that are in contact.

The time record in case of water is less than that in case of glycerin.

Viscosity  
It is the property of fluid due to existence of friction force between each liquid layer and the 
adjacent one, which resists the sliding

Temperature and thermal energy 
Introduction  
The terms (temperature) and (heat) are often used interchangeably in everyday language. In 
physics, however, these two terms have very different meanings.  
We’ll define temperature in terms of how it’s measured and see how temperature changes 
affect the dimensions of objects. We’ll see that heat

ct the dimensions of objects. We’ll see that heat refers to energy transfer caused by 
temperature differences. 
The concept of temperature is rooted in qualitative ideas of “hot” and “cold” based on our 
sense of touch. A body that feels hot usually has a higher temperature than a similar body that 
feels cold.  
Concept of Heat: 
(It is thermal energy transferred from hotter system to cooler system that are in 
contact).
